items.question: Which divine forms protect the private parts and the back?
premises: The conqueror of senses is invoked to protect the private part
The best of the Raghus is invoked to protect the back
items.inference: Different epithets of Rāma guard specific body parts
items.plain_english: May the conqueror of the senses protect the private parts; may the best of the Raghus protect the back.

items.question: Who is invoked to protect the thighs and destroy demon families?
premises: The thighs require divine protection
The best of the Raghus is the destroyer of demon families
items.inference: Rāma as destroyer of demons protects the thighs
items.plain_english: May the best of the Raghus, the destroyer of the demon families, protect the thighs.

items.question: Which aspects of Rāma protect the feet and the entire body?
premises: The giver of prosperity to Vibhīṣaṇa is invoked to protect the feet
Rāma is invoked to protect the entire body
items.inference: Rāma’s beneficent power extends protection to all parts of the body
items.plain_english: May the giver of prosperity to Vibhīṣaṇa protect the feet; may Rāma protect the entire body.

items.question: What benefits arise for one who receives Rāma’s protection?
premises: The protected person becomes long-lived and happy
The protected person becomes endowed with sons, victory, and humility
items.inference: Rāma’s protection yields comprehensive worldly and personal well-being
items.plain_english: He becomes long-lived, happy, blessed with sons, victorious, and humble.

items.question: Can hostile beings even look upon one protected by Rāma’s names?
premises: Protection is effected by Rāma’s names
Hostile beings lack the power to even see the protected person
items.inference: The names of Rāma provide an inviolable shield against adversaries
items.plain_english: Those protected by the names of Rāma cannot even be seen by them.

items.question: What spiritual and worldly outcomes result from being protected by Rāma’s names?
premises: The person is not tainted by sins
The person obtains both enjoyment and liberation
items.inference: Protection by Rāma’s names grants freedom from sin and the dual goals of life
items.plain_english: A person is not tainted by sins and obtains both enjoyment and liberation.

items.question: What accomplishments come to one who holds this in the hand?
premises: A person may hold this in the hand
All accomplishments become situated in that person’s hand
items.inference: Holding this confers immediate access to all accomplishments
uncertainties: The specific object to be held is implied from context
items.plain_english: For whoever holds it in the hand, all accomplishments are placed within reach.

items.question: What result follows from making and holding this sacred object?
premises: One may make and hold this object
Such a person obtains the desired fruit
items.inference: Ritual preparation and retention of this object fulfill one’s desires
uncertainties: The specific object is implied from context
items.plain_english: Whoever makes it and holds it indeed obtains the desired fruit.

items.question: What assured benefit accrues to a woman through this practice?
premises: She becomes endowed with many children
Her offspring remain alive and there is no doubt
items.inference: The practice guarantees fertility and the survival of offspring
items.plain_english: She becomes the mother of many children with living offspring; there is no doubt about this.

items.question: What authority and auspicious success does the practitioner obtain everywhere?
premises: The practitioner gains unobstructed command everywhere
The practitioner obtains victory and auspiciousness
items.inference: The practice confers universal authority and auspicious victory
items.plain_english: One obtains unobstructed command everywhere and attains victory and auspiciousness.

items.question: Who recorded this revelation upon awakening in the morning?
premises: The wise Kauśika awakened in the morning
He wrote it down as revealed
items.inference: The sage Budha Kauśika transmitted the revelation by writing it after awakening
items.plain_english: Thus the wise Kauśika, awakened in the morning, wrote it down.

items.question: Which heroic pair is invoked to grant protection on the path?
premises: The two heroes Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa are invoked
They are asked to protect the speaker on the path
items.inference: Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa together serve as guardians during travel
items.plain_english: May both heroes, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, protect me on the path.

items.question: What physical and ascetic attributes characterize Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa here?
premises: They have wide lotus-like eyes
They are clad in bark garments and black antelope skin
items.inference: The pair is depicted with divine beauty and ascetic attire
items.plain_english: The two with wide lotus-like eyes, clad in bark garments and black antelope skin.

items.question: What familial identities define the protective pair Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa?
premises: They are the two sons of Daśaratha
They are brothers named Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa
items.inference: The invoked protectors are identified by their royal lineage and brotherhood
items.plain_english: These two sons of Daśaratha, the brothers Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa.

items.question: How do Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa act as protectors against demonic forces?
premises: They are destroyers of demon families
They are invoked to protect you
items.inference: The best of the Raghus safeguard devotees by destroying demonic threats
items.plain_english: May the two destroyers of demon families, the best of the Raghus, protect you.

items.question: Who is asked to protect us and fulfill our heart’s desire?
premises: Rāma together with Lakṣmaṇa is invoked
He is asked to protect us and fulfill our desire
items.inference: Rāma accompanied by Lakṣmaṇa grants both protection and fulfillment of wishes
items.plain_english: May Rāma, together with Lakṣmaṇa, protect us and fulfill our heart’s desire.

items.question: What weapons characterize Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa as protectors?
premises: Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa bear bows
They are equipped with arrows
items.inference: The protective pair is depicted as fully armed warriors
items.plain_english: Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, bearing bows and arrows.

items.question: What lineage and supreme qualities define Rāma in this praise?
premises: Rāma is a descendant of Kakutstha and son of Kausalyā
He is the supreme, perfect person and best of the Raghus
items.inference: Rāma unites royal lineage with supreme and perfect divine nature
items.plain_english: The descendant of Kakutstha, the supreme person, perfect, son of Kausalyā, the best of the Raghus.

items.question: What relational and heroic qualities distinguish Rāma’s glory?
premises: Rāma is the beloved of Jānakī and glorious
He possesses immeasurable prowess
items.inference: Rāma’s glory combines loving devotion and limitless heroic power
items.plain_english: The beloved of Jānakī, glorious, of immeasurable prowess.

items.question: Why is the best of the Raghus saluted with Hanumān before him?
premises: The son of the wind stands before him
The speaker bows to that best of the Raghus
items.inference: Rāma is revered as the supreme lord attended by Hanumān
items.plain_english: I bow to that best of the Raghus, before whom stands the son of the wind.

items.question: How is repeated reverence expressed toward Śrī Rāma’s virtuous nature?
premises: Śrī Rāma delights in virtues
The speaker bows to him again and again
items.inference: Rāma’s virtuous nature inspires continual and repeated devotion
items.plain_english: I bow again and again to Śrī Rāma, who delights in virtues.

items.question: What immense merit is assured to one who engages in this devotion?
premises: One obtains the merit of ten thousand horse sacrifices
There is no doubt about this result
items.inference: The devotion yields merit equal to vast Vedic sacrifices without uncertainty
items.plain_english: He obtains the merit of ten thousand horse sacrifices; there is no doubt.

items.question: What kind of supreme devotion is sought at Rāma’s lotus feet?
premises: The prayer seeks devotion attached to the dust of Rāma’s lotus feet
This devotion is described as supreme
items.inference: The highest devotion is humble attachment to Rāma’s lotus feet
items.plain_english: Grant me supreme devotion, devoted to the dust of your lotus feet.

items.question: What grace is requested from the immeasurable destroyer of sorrow?
premises: The immeasurable supreme person is addressed
He is asked to be gracious as the destroyer of our sorrow
items.inference: The devotee seeks compassionate grace from the supreme remover of suffering
items.plain_english: O immeasurable one, be gracious, O destroyer of our sorrows, O supreme person.
